source_review.notes: Checked all 14 structured references against current official W3C DCAT/PROV, DCMI, Schema.org, DataCite, OpenLineage, dbt, DataHub, OpenMetadata, Apache Atlas, Bitol ODCS, OpenTelemetry, and Google SRE sources. Verified dataset/catalog vocabulary, provenance, persistent description, entity/aspect/type models, manifest/catalog artifacts, run/resource identity, contracts, ingestion/search/lineage/classification architecture, and operational monitoring in their stated scopes; all final URLs returned HTTP 200.

evidence: Checked symbols for stable entity/assertion sets, assertion tuple, technical/operational/business projections, consumer question, compatibility predicates, coverage, valid interval, observation time, confidence, and classification.
Checked suitability conjunction, assertion-resolution set comprehension, coverage ratio, typed tuple components, and proof equalities for defined symbols and balanced syntax.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation consistently separates subject identity, predicate/value, provenance/authority, temporal scope, confidence/protection, view projection, compatibility, and coverage.

evidence: Executed metadata-view-selection and matched two technical matches, false unique identification, one business match, one operationally ready product, and finance.daily_net selection exactly.

Verified both products use identical two-field schema, while only the net-recognized/USD concept passes business requirements and its 15-minute age plus approved quality satisfy the 60-minute operational bound.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The executable correctly demonstrates why shape compatibility alone does not identify semantic and operational fitness.

evidence: Verified Suitable(e,q,t) conjoins rather than substitutes technical, operational, and business compatibility for the stated consumer use.
Verified Current(e,p,t) selects valid-time-compatible assertions before applying predicate-specific resolution over authority, provenance, scope, approval, confidence, staleness, and conflicts.
Confirmed coverage becomes unknown when the eligible denominator is unknown rather than being assigned a misleading numeric ratio.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Formal claims preserve projection, temporal validity, authority, evidence provenance, conflict, and coverage assumptions.

evidence: Reviewed environment/tenant collisions, rename/move/split/merge/reuse, independent component versions, late observations, out-of-order/duplicate/missing events, collector upgrades, parser bugs, and source replay.

Reviewed declared-versus-observed conflict, stale owner/group membership, null/absent/unknown/unauthorized distinctions, unknown denominators, access-log gaps, manual exports, inferred metadata, and catalog/source drift.

Reviewed sensitive names/query text/samples/lineage/usage, existence leaks through search/facets/counts/edges/errors, cache authorization, active-action races, retirement aliases/consumers/policies, legal hold, redaction, and derived indexes.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Adversarial analysis covers identity, time, provenance, authority, collection, resolution, authorization, automation, lifecycle, and deletion failure surfaces.

evidence: Traced stable entities, aliases/incarnations, typed assertions, source/method, claim-specific authority, valid/observed time, technical/operational/business projections, conflicts, coverage, access and lifecycle through exposition, examples, and answers.

Confirmed source assertions remain preserved when a current projection is resolved, crawler observations cannot overwrite curated semantics, and declared/observed/inferred/curated claims remain labeled.
Confirmed active actions re-read current versions/policy/authorization and use scope, idempotency, receipt and rollback while retirement propagates across aliases, indexes, consumers and controls.
invariant_checking.notes: No name, crawl, latest timestamp, schema match, glossary definition, job success, access-log absence, popularity rank, inferred owner, tag, or catalog badge is described as stronger evidence than it supplies.

evidence: Reviewed the seven-step counterexample with two datasets having identical technical schema but gross-booked versus net-recognized meanings.

Confirmed a consumer requirement for current net recognized revenue cannot be distinguished by equal technical projections, while business compatibility rejects gross and operational evidence admits the current approved net product.
Confirmed the conclusion is limited to insufficiency of technical metadata for requirements that include meaning and current condition.
proof_review.notes: The counterexample validly disproves semantic identity and fitness as consequences of technical equality alone.

evidence: The technical-insufficiency argument is explicitly labeled a proof sketch.
The following limitation states that not every decision requires every possible metadata field.
The executable is described as a deterministic selection model rather than evidence that one universal recommender can infer fitness.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Proof, model choice, consumer-specific requirement, deterministic example, and limitations remain explicit.

evidence: Current vocabulary, provenance, catalog/artifact, metadata-model, resource-identity, contract, and monitoring behaviors are attributed to dated primary sources.
The executable explicitly disclaims catalog, ontology-reasoner, resolver, freshness-service, access-control, and universal-recommender behavior.

Declared, observed, parsed, inferred, curated, computed, overridden, current, unknown, stale, and conflicting claims are labeled with provenance, authority, time, confidence, coverage, or access limits.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Standards, project implementations, deterministic illustration, observed evidence, curated meaning, inference, and policy resolution are kept distinct.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed the chapter end to end. It integrates technical, operational, and business projections around stable versioned entities; provenance-bearing temporal assertions; claim-specific authority and visible conflict; replayable collection; precise semantics; operational state; access-filtered serving; guarded active metadata; and secure quality/lifecycle governance without treating a catalog snapshot as universal truth.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed the assertion record, identity/version/effectivity model, source-of-record matrix, event-plus-snapshot collection, raw/normalized evidence, coverage and reconciliation, ownership roles, business definition template, run/publication state, search/API surfaces, authorization filtering, active-action guardrails, metadata SLOs, deprecation, retirement, and five production exercises.

pedagogical_review.notes: Reviewed progression from the one-page three-view model through identity/time, provenance/authority, collection, business semantics, operational state, serving, governance, formal suitability/resolution/coverage, proof counterexample, executable, 12 trade-offs, 30 misconceptions, ten examples, cross-program links, and five exercises with detailed answers. limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
